title: Scalar extension respects the open base-change comparison
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U'&\xrightarrow h&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow g&X\end{array}$$
be an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], with arbitrary $g$. Use ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $S_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and let $\lambda_u:u_B^{-1}S_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S_Tu_A^{-1}$ be the canonical K-flat tensor inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Use the exact open extensions $j_!^R\dashv j_R^{-1}$, with unit $\eta_j^R$, for $R=A,B$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $\beta_j:S_Xj_!^A\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^BS_U$ be the isomorphism of left adjoints obtained from the identity between their right adjoints $j_A^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_X=\operatorname{Res}_Uj_B^{-1}$, with scalar restriction as in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Equivalently $\beta_{j,K}^{-1}$ is the $j_!^B\dashv j_B^{-1}$ adjunct of
$$S_UK\xrightarrow{S_U\eta_{j,K}^A}S_Uj_A^{-1}j_!^AK\xrightarrow{\lambda_{j,j_!^AK}^{-1}}j_B^{-1}S_Xj_!^AK.$$
Define $\beta_{j'}$ in the same way. Write $e_j^R:g_R^{-1}j_!^R\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^Rh_R^{-1}$ for the actual base-change map of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Its inverse is the $j'_!{}^R\dashv j_R'{}^{-1}$ adjunct of $h_R^{-1}\eta_j^R$, followed by the cartesian inverse-image identification. Then for every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$$j'_!{}^B(\lambda_{h,K})\circ e_{j,S_UK}^B\circ g_B^{-1}(\beta_{j,K})
=\beta_{j',h_A^{-1}K}\circ S_{X'}(e_{j,K}^A)\circ\lambda_{g,j_!^AK}.$$
This is an equality in $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ from $g_B^{-1}S_Xj_!^AK$ to $j'_!{}^BS_{U'}h_A^{-1}K$, natural in $K$. No flatness or finite projective-dimension hypothesis on $B$ over $A$ is imposed.

proof.text: For each $T$, [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] gives $S_T\dashv\operatorname{Res}_T$ on the ordinary unbounded categories, with unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ on K-flat representatives. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], $j_!^R\dashv j_R^{-1}$. The two composite left adjoints $S_Xj_!^A$ and $j_!^BS_U$ therefore have right adjoints $j_A^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_X$ and $\operatorname{Res}_Uj_B^{-1}$, identified by the inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Taking the adjoint of this identity gives the canonical isomorphism $\beta_j$; the inverse identity gives its inverse, since the adjunction bijections [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and triangle identities carry their composites to identities. This is the specified normalization: under the scalar adjunction the tensor inverse-image comparison preserves $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, so transposing $\beta_j^{-1}$ under $j_!^B\dashv j_B^{-1}$ gives exactly $\delta_j=\lambda_j^{-1}\circ S_U\eta_j^A$ in the statement. For an object $M$ on $X$, the comparison between restriction and $j^{-1}$ is the scalar-adjoint transpose of $\lambda_{j,M}^{-1}$: on a K-flat model of $M$ both unit formulas are $j^{-1}x\mapsto j^{-1}x\otimes1$. Applying this at $M=j_!^AK$ and composing with the open unit gives the displayed $\delta_j$, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The same construction gives $\beta_{j'}$.

Use abbreviations $F_R=j_!^R$, $F'_R=j'_!{}^R$, $J_R=j_R^{-1}$, $J'_R=j_R'{}^{-1}$, $G_R=g_R^{-1}$ and $H_R=h_R^{-1}$. Identify $J'_RG_R=H_RJ_R$ by the cartesian inverse-image comparison. The canonical tensor comparisons satisfy
$$J'_B\lambda_g^{-1}\circ\lambda_{j'}^{-1}G_A=H_B\lambda_j^{-1}\circ\lambda_h^{-1}J_A.\tag{C}$$
Here both sides go from $S_{U'}J'_AG_A$ to $J'_BG_BS_X$. This is the composition identity for these particular tensor maps: choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ on $X$. The inverse images remain K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. In each degree both paths send the local generator $(gj')^{-1}p\otimes b$ to $(gj')^{-1}(p\otimes b)$, with $gj'=jh$; the balanced tensor relations and restrictions are identical. Thus the maps of tensor complexes agree and give (C) in the derived category. The same formula shows naturality of each $\lambda_u$ in its input.

proof.text:
Let $L$ and $R$ be the left and right composites in the asserted equality, and put $N=F_AK$. They are isomorphisms by step 1, the tensor comparison, and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Their inverses are
$$L^{-1}=G_B(\beta_j^{-1})\circ(e_j^B)^{-1}\circ F'_B(\lambda_h^{-1}),\qquad R^{-1}=\lambda_g^{-1}\circ S_{X'}((e_j^A)^{-1})\circ\beta_{j'}^{-1}.$$
Both have source $F'_BS_{U'}H_AK$ and target $G_BS_XN$, so they can be transposed under $F'_B\dashv J'_B$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The inverse of the actual canonical $e_j^R$ has transpose $H_R\eta_j^R$ by [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars], applied with the identity coefficient map $R\to R$. Its complex-level unit formula descends termwise to the derived category because the open extensions and identified-coefficient inverse images are exact. Consequently the transpose of $L^{-1}$ is
$$J'_BG_B(\beta_{j,K}^{-1})\circ H_B(\eta^B_{j,S_UK})\circ\lambda_{h,K}^{-1}
=H_B(\delta_{j,K})\circ\lambda_{h,K}^{-1}.$$
For the equality use $J'_BG_B=H_BJ_B$ and the defining adjunct equation $J_B(\beta_j^{-1})\circ\eta_j^B=\delta_j$. This transposes the inverses, whose source is an open extension, rather than the original maps whose target is an open extension.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); inverse-map unit normalization and adjunction naturality; the exact inverse-mate normalization is the statement of lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars.

proof.text:
The transpose of $R^{-1}$ under the same adjunction is
$$J'_B(\lambda_{g,N}^{-1})\circ J'_BS_{X'}((e_{j,K}^A)^{-1})\circ\delta_{j',H_AK}.$$
Substitute $\delta_{j',H_AK}=\lambda_{j',F'_AH_AK}^{-1}\circ S_{U'}(\eta^A_{j',H_AK})$. Naturality of $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}$ moves $(e_{j,K}^A)^{-1}$ past it, and the inverse normalization of [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] gives
$$J'_A((e_{j,K}^A)^{-1})\circ\eta^A_{j',H_AK}=H_A(\eta^A_{j,K}).$$
Thus the transpose is exactly
$$J'_B(\lambda_{g,N}^{-1})\circ\lambda_{j',G_AN}^{-1}\circ S_{U'}H_A(\eta^A_{j,K}).$$
All these are equalities of morphisms in $D(U'_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, using only naturality and the two specified unit normalizations [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; the canonical open comparison is the one in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change].

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); explicit right-composite inverse transpose; the exact inverse-mate normalization is the statement of lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars.

proof.text:
Apply (C) at $N$ to the last formula. It becomes
$$H_B(\lambda_{j,N}^{-1})\circ\lambda_{h,J_AN}^{-1}\circ S_{U'}H_A(\eta^A_{j,K})
=H_B(\lambda_{j,N}^{-1})\circ H_BS_U(\eta^A_{j,K})\circ\lambda_{h,K}^{-1}
=H_B(\delta_{j,K})\circ\lambda_{h,K}^{-1}.$$
The middle equality is precisely naturality of $\lambda_h^{-1}$ on $\eta^A_{j,K}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. This is the transpose computed for $L^{-1}$ in step 3. The adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives $L^{-1}=R^{-1}$ and hence $L=R$, the displayed equality in $D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. Every map used is natural in $K$. K-flat representatives and exact inverse images work for unbounded complexes and arbitrary $A\to B$; no flatness of $B$ or finite projective-dimension hypothesis has entered.
